_comment: Committed, path-free selection for the Qwen3.8-27B quantization showdown. Machine paths, sizes, and checksums live in the GENERATED manifest written by scripts/showdown_acquire.py. Do not put local paths here.

_arch_notes: Hybrid attention: 64 text layers, layer_types alternate three 'linear_attention' layers then one 'full_attention' (full_attention_interval=4). Only 16 layers hold a conventional KV cache; the rest carry a recurrent linear-attention state.
Consequence: KV-cache growth with context is roughly a quarter of a comparable all-full-attention 27B, so KV quantization buys far less here than on a standard dense model. Measure it; do not assume.
Multimodal: vision_config present, image_token_id/video_token_id defined. mlx_lm.server loads it as text fine (verified locally); GGUF carries a separate mmproj.

Model-card sampling: temperature=1.0, top_p=0.95, top_k=20 (generation_config.json). The repository catalog's qwen3_27b_dense entry pins temp=0.7/top_p=0.95/top_k=20 for non-thinking agent use; the showdown uses temperature=0.0 for scored evals and records the value used.

mlx_lm.speculative_draft: --draft-model exists but no qwen3_5_mtp implementation in mlx_lm.models
mlx_lm._note: This is the daily-serving path (:8085, Pi, Mycelium). Native fp16 KV only.

mlx_vlm._note: KV quantization and MTP are ONLY available here. Any KV or MTP arm therefore needs an mlx_vlm KV-native control arm, or server and KV mode are confounded.

llama_cpp._note: serve_local.sh defaults to -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0. That is a KV-quantized default, so the llama.cpp KV-native control arm must pass -ctk f16 -ctv f16 explicitly.

artifacts.quant_method: mlx affine, group_size=64, bits=4, uniform (no per-module overrides)
artifacts._note: Already on disk. Bottom of the single-provider uniform ladder.
Hypothesis: daily-driver sweet spot. Designed to be falsifiable against 5bit and oQ4.
Already on disk. Quality reference for the MLX path.

artifacts.quant_method: oQ mixed precision (oMLX v0.6.0rc1), affine base bits=4 group_size=64 with 161 per-module bit overrides
artifacts._note: Sensitivity-aware counterpart to mlx_lms_4bit at near-identical footprint (4.86 vs 4.69 bpw). The controlled test of allocation-vs-uniform at the memory-constrained end. The ARTIFACT is ordinary MLX safetensors loadable by mlx_lm/mlx_vlm; using it does NOT reintroduce oMLX as a serving path, which stays retired.

artifacts.quant_method: mlx affine group_size=64 bits=4; model_type qwen3_5_mtp
artifacts._note: Drafter head only (~0.24 GB), not a standalone model. Pairs with an MLX target via mlx_vlm.server --draft-model --draft-kind mtp. mlx_lm has no qwen3_5_mtp implementation at 0.31.3, so this is an mlx_vlm-only arm.

artifacts.quant_method: mlx affine group_size=64 bits=8; model_type qwen3_5_mtp

artifacts._note: Single-provider GGUF ladder base. bartowski is the only reputable source carrying the complete Q4_K_M/Q5_K_M/Q6_K set for this model.

artifacts.quant_method: llama-quantize Q4_K_M, no imatrix (16.81 GB vs bartowski's 17.44 GB for the same nominal quant)
artifacts._note: Already on disk. Zero-cost control for 'two files labelled Q4_K_M are not the same file'. Any measured gap between this and gguf_bartowski_q4_k_m is a conversion-recipe effect, not a quant-level effect.
Official ggml-org MTP draft head for llama.cpp --spec-type draft-mtp. Vocab compatibility with a bartowski target is same-base-model but must be proven at smoke time, not assumed.
Not queued by default. MLX-8bit already provides a high-precision reference and costs no download. Add with --tier optional if the GGUF ladder needs its own ceiling.

artifacts.quant_method: abliterated weights then llama-quantize Q6_K; 22.43 GB, byte-for-byte the same size as the stock lmstudio-community Q6_K, indicating the same quant recipe
artifacts.modification: refusal ablation (remove-refusals-with-transformers), layers 18-51 only; model card states MTP and vision heads unmodified
artifacts.selection_rationale: Highest adoption of the five candidates (2.83M downloads, 784 likes) and the only one still being updated (2026-09-18). Single-axis modification with a documented layer range, standard packaging, no patched runtime required.
artifacts._note: Deferred tier. Pick its quant AFTER the core ladder identifies the best standard precision; Q6_K is the default placeholder, overridable with --quant.

artifacts.quant_method: abliterated weights then llama-quantize Q6_K; 22.43 GB, same size as stock Q6_K
artifacts.modification: refusal_direction_ablation, method=aggressive, 5 SVD directions, whitened SVD, norm-preserving, 3 refinement passes, layer_selection=knee_cosmic with min_layer_fraction 0.4 (from the repo's own abliteration_metadata.json)
artifacts.selection_rationale: The only candidate publishing a full machine-readable record of its own modification, plus a hard_negative_residue.json. 1260 likes. Its bf16 safetensors also permit a later MLX conversion if a same-serving-path comparison is wanted.

rejected_candidates.reason: Best provenance packaging of the five (Ed25519-signed FastMTP-PROVENANCE.json, SHA256SUMS, release manifest) but it ships HauhauCS-FastMTP-llama.cpp.patch, i.e. FastMTP needs a patched llama.cpp. That fails the 'compatible with the serving path we intend to test' bar and would make its results non-comparable against stock llama-server arms. Reconsider only as a dedicated FastMTP study.

105 GGUF files under an unrelated 'RVN-*' naming scheme that does not match the repo or model name, plus xet_speed_test.bin and xet_test_100mb.bin committed into the repo. Packaging hygiene is too poor to trust an unexplained artifact selection.

Its base_model is itself a DavidAU multi-stage merge, not stock Qwen3.8-27B. Several modifications (merge, Heretic, NEO-CODER tuning, MTP) are stacked at once, so a measured difference cannot be attributed to any one of them. Interesting model; unusable as a controlled derivative comparison.
